newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy rescues illegal immigrants in sinking ship.
newsitem.headline: Italy rescues illegal immigrants in sinking ship.

text.p: About 100 illegal immigrants were rescued from a ship that was sinking off the coast of southern Italy on Friday in the latest emergency to strike a tide of economic refugees desperate to start a new life in the West.
Italy's maritime rescue coordination centre said the Turkish ship, reported to be made of wood, had sent out a distress signal.
It was found two miles off the coast on the heel of Italy after a sea and air search and was being towed to the port of Gallipoli, the centre said in a statement.
The vessel, named by Italian news agencies as the Manolia, had a human cargo of Sri Lankans and Iranians, the centre said. "The people on board appear to be in good health," it said.
Reports from Gallipoli said the illegal immigrants were being ferried to shore in coastguard vessels and a flotilla of small boats, including pleasure craft.
A coastguard official said the ship, believed to be about 30 metres (100 feet) long, had a gash in its side and had taken in water.
Thousands of illegal immigrants pour in to Italy crammed into small boats at great risk and high cost.
The southern Adriatic coast and the remote island of Lampedusa, midway between Sicily and North Africa, are favoured entry points.

Illegal immigrants caught by coastguards and police are served with expulsion orders. Authorities acknowledge, however, that many of the foreigners ignore the notice and stay in Italy or try to move on to other European countries.
